candidates.title: Salesforce gives Agentforce a long-horizon runtime
candidates.summary: The runtime keeps goals running across days and weeks with persistent memory, durable execution, and dynamic steering.
candidates.what_changed: Salesforce introduced a long-horizon runtime for Agentforce so an agent can pursue a business goal over days or weeks instead of a single chat session.
candidates.why_it_matters: Long-running agents need explicit lifecycle semantics. Persistence, resumability, approvals, and course correction become product requirements once the unit of work lasts longer than one interaction.

candidates.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows makes MCP calls visible in logs
candidates.summary: The gh-aw release records MCP server and tool names per call, strengthening observability for agentic CI workflows.
candidates.what_changed: GitHub's Agentic Workflows project added more structured observability to `gh aw logs`, including identifiable MCP server and tool names for individual tool calls.
candidates.why_it_matters: Agent observability should preserve tool identity and execution provenance by default. Logs are part of the control plane, not a debugging afterthought.

candidates.title: Harness or model? A private benchmark separates the two
candidates.summary: A contamination-controlled study finds no clear average winner between native and neutral coding-agent harnesses, while showing large task-specific and cost differences.
candidates.what_changed: This study asks a question coding-agent benchmarks often blur: how much performance comes from the model, and how much from the harness around it?
candidates.why_it_matters: A coding-agent evaluation that names only the model is incomplete. Tool design, prompts, control flow, recovery, and context handling can shift results enough to change practical conclusions.

sources.label: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding

candidates.title: K-Bench shows model unlearning can fail once the model becomes an agent
candidates.summary: The benchmark checks chain-of-thought, tools, observations, and summaries—not just final answers—and finds secrets can still leak through agent channels.
candidates.what_changed: K-Bench challenges a convenient assumption in machine unlearning: if the final answer no longer reveals a fact, the system has forgotten it.
candidates.why_it_matters: Privacy and deletion guarantees need to be evaluated at the **agent-system level**. Retrieval stores, prompts, traces, and tool outputs can preserve knowledge that the base-model evaluation misses.

sources.label: K-Bench: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning in Agentic Deployments
